text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwean government, reeling under a Z$6.6 billion budget deficit, has all the same purchased 48 Mercedes Benz luxury vehicles worth Z$35 million and a fleet of Peugeot 405 and Mazda 626 cars for use by foreign heads of state and their spouses expected to attend the World Solar Summit in Harare later this month.
- The chairman of the Zimbabwe Council for Tourism says the sector must widen its product base if it is to encourage more visitors to come and stay in the country longer.

- Property agents in Zimbabwe say the recently ended strike by civil servants severely disrupted their cash-flow because the deeds office where all property transactions are verified was closed during the strike.

- A draft national plan of action aimed at speeding up Zimbabwe's housing delivery system by broadening the finance base, minimising constraints and bringing about competitiveness to help lower building cost was unveiled in the capital Harare on Thursday.

- A row is brewing over an instruction to all heads of ministries in the Zimbabwean government to compile a list of all civil servants who defied a call to return to work on August 23 after going on strike for wage rises, but whose consequent dismissal was later revoked by cabinet.
